Topic 7.1: Oral Literature 7.1.1 Performance in Oral Literature
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Oral Literature 7.1.1 Performance in Oral Literature, part of PERFORMANCE IN ORAL LITERATURE Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Sugg in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How does performance affect the subject matter in oral literature?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Oral Literature 7.1.1 Performance in Oral Literature together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: This is nurtured as the learner interacts with digital content when searching online or offline for

features of a good performance and presents findings in class.

● Creativity and imagination: This is enhanced as the learner embraces ideas that inspire creativity when performing an

oral literature piece using the performance techniques.

Values:
● Integrity: This is enhanced as the learner gives honest and constructive feedback when reviewing each other’s

performance for creativity and correctness.

● Peace: This is advanced as the learner tolerates peers when watching the performance of any of the forms of oral

literature and identifying performance techniques applied.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life skills (self-awareness): This is nurtured as the learner exhibits individual skills and audience awareness to perform

an oral literature piece using performance techniques acquired.
